who: Historian of modern Armenia at the University of Michigan; doctorate from UCLA.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Gerard J. Libaridian as the modern Armenian history professor at Michigan, Ann Arbor, during 2000–2012.
Michigan renewed Gerard J. Libaridian’s modern Armenian history professorship for 2007–2012 and states that he earned his doctorate at UCLA.
The indexed title page of Richard Edward Antaramian’s 2014 Michigan history dissertation names retired Visiting Professor Gerard Libaridian as co-chair.
The catalogue identifies Gerard Jirair Libaridian’s UCLA doctoral thesis, The ideology of Armenian liberation, with copyright 1987 and a 1988 microfilm reproduction.

notes: Name, institution, field and student agree. The AHA year 1988 differs from the thesis copyright year 1987; the catalogue also records a 1988 reproduction.

who: Historian of modern Eastern Europe at UT Austin; PhD in history, Toronto, 2009.

evidence.says: The authority for the author of Zionists in interwar Czechoslovakia identifies Tatjana Lichtenstein as an assistant professor of history at UT Austin.
Lichtenstein’s university-hosted CV lists a Toronto history PhD in 2009 and an appointment in modern Eastern European history at UT Austin beginning in 2009.
UT identifies Tatjana Lichtenstein as an associate professor of modern Eastern European history, with a Toronto PhD in 2009, and lists Zionists in Interwar Czechoslovakia among her works.

notes: Exact name, doctoral institution and year, UT appointment and book identity agree.

who: Historian of modern Britain and empire at Mississippi; PhD in history, Northwestern, 2016.

evidence.says: The authority for Working-class Raj identifies Alexandra Lindgren-Gibson as assistant professor of history at the University of Mississippi.
Mississippi’s faculty profile identifies Alexandra Lindgren-Gibson, author of Working-Class Raj, as a historian of modern Britain and empire and lists her Northwestern history PhD in 2016.

notes: Exact name, university, doctorate and publication connect the LC author to the supervisor.

who: Alberto A. Martínez, historian of science and mathematics at UT Austin; PhD, Minnesota.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Alberto A. Martínez, author of Negative math and Science secrets, as teaching history of science and mathematics at UT Austin.
John Lisle’s university-hosted CV lists his 2019 UT history doctorate and the supplied Science and Espionage dissertation, with Alberto A. Martínez as advisor.
Martínez’s 2019 CV lists UT appointments from 2005, a Minnesota history of science and technology PhD in 2001, and John Lisle as his dissertation supervisee.
The 2014–2015 UT catalogue lists Alberto A. Martinez in history with a Minnesota–Twin Cities PhD in 2000.

notes: Direct student evidence selects Alberto A. Martínez from the namesakes. UT sources disagree between 2000 (matching AHA) and 2001 for the doctorate year; institution and field agree.

who: Wilfred M. McClay, historian of the United States and former Tulane faculty member; PhD in history, Johns Hopkins, 1987.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Wilfred M. McClay, author of The Masterless and Land of hope, and records his history PhD from Johns Hopkins.
Tulane lists Michael L. Andrews’s 2005 Thomas Jefferson and the Endless Republic dissertation with Wilfred M. McClay as committee chair.
The biography gives his Johns Hopkins history PhD as 1987 and records that he taught at Tulane before moving to Tennessee at Chattanooga in 1999.

notes: Tulane explicitly supplies the supervisor’s full name for the exact student and dissertation. His departure before the completion year does not undermine this direct identification.

who: James C. McClelland, historian at Nebraska–Lincoln from 1979; PhD, Princeton, 1970.

evidence.says: The authority for James C. McClelland’s Autocrats and academics records a Princeton PhD and an earlier history appointment at UC Santa Barbara.
Nebraska’s 2002–2004 history faculty list includes James C. McClelland, appointed in 1979 and then professor emeritus, with a Princeton PhD in 1970.
Nebraska’s history department identifies James McClelland as an emeritus history professor.

notes: The contemporaneous Nebraska bulletin supplies the middle initial and exact doctoral institution and year, identifying the LC candidate despite its older Santa Barbara affiliation.

who: Tracy McDonald, historian of Russia and the Soviet Union at McMaster; PhD, Toronto.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Tracy McDonald as an associate professor of history at McMaster specializing in Russian and Soviet history, citing McMaster’s faculty page in 2019.
McMaster’s 2019 museum event identifies Tracy McDonald as an associate professor of history and author of Face to the Village: The Riazan Countryside under Soviet Rule, 1921–1930.
McMaster’s history faculty listing records Tracy McDonald as an associate professor with a Toronto PhD.
The alternative authority’s ECIP source note identifies its author as Lynn Tracy McDonald; it provides no connection to the McMaster historian.

notes: The McMaster affiliation, Russian/Soviet field and Toronto doctorate agree. The alternative n2011031508 authority concerns a different author. Doctorate year was not independently verified.

who: Ernest William McDonnell, professor of medieval studies at Rutgers; PhD, Wisconsin, 1947.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Ernest William McDonnell, also appearing as Ernest W. McDonnell, through Jacob van Maerlant (1947), recording a Wisconsin PhD in 1947.
New Brunswick Theological Seminary’s Sage Library identifies Ernest W. McDonnell as a scholar and professor of medieval studies at Rutgers University.

notes: The full-name authority’s exact Wisconsin doctorate and year, together with the Rutgers medieval studies appointment, identify the candidate.
